To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present bowtie networks for joint few-shot recognition (FSR) and novel-view synthesis (NVS), which are able to learn 3D semantic representations and generate high-quality images from novel viewpoints, and we demonstrate that such synthesized images are effective for improving the performance of FSR.

we propose bowtie neural networks that simultaneously perform novel view synthesis and object classification, which is a novel and challenging problem, and that we achieve significant improvements over the state-of-the-art in both tasks.
We introduce bowtie networks that learn 3D representations for joint few-shot recognition of novel object categories and novel-view synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning representations for images, with the goal of enabling the recognition of novel object classes from few examples, and the generation of novel images from new viewpoints.

the following two questions: (1) How to improve recognition of novel categories with only a few training examples? (2) How to generate images from new viewpoints of novel categories? We propose bowtie networks to simultaneously answer these two questions.

(1) We introduce a new problem of joint few-shot learning of recognition and view synthesis.

we propose to learn joint representations of 3D geometry and semantics for few-shot recognition and view synthesis, which is achieved by a feedback loop between a generative and a discriminative task.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the interaction and feedback between generative and discriminative models can help both tasks to benefit from each other, and that the proposed architecture is a promising framework to study such interaction.
the generative and discriminative models are complementary to each other, and they can be trained in a way that benefits from their interaction.
we can leverage the generative model for the discriminative model and vice versa, and this is especially beneficial for low data regimes.
